title: Factorization existence for a stable pullback image
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category, $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories, and $V$ a cocone such that its object and arrow set cocones are colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Fix $j\in J$, $f:Y\to X$ and $g:Z\to X$ in $F(j)$ admitting a pullback $P=Y\times_X Z$, with projections $p:P\to Y$ and $q:P\to Z$. Assume every transition out of $j$ preserves this pullback. Write $U_j$ for the cocone functor $F(j)\to V.\mathrm{pt}$. For every object $W$ of $V.\mathrm{pt}$ and arrows $a:W\to U_j(Y)$ and $b:W\to U_j(Z)$ with $U_j(f)\circ a=U_j(g)\circ b$, there exists $l:W\to U_j(P)$ satisfying $U_j(p)\circ l=a$ and $U_j(q)\circ l=b$. No uniqueness is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites), pullback paragraph and displayed Hom calculation; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YL

proof.text:
Lift the vertex and two legs using joint surjectivity of the object and
arrow set colimits. Pass to a common stage above these representatives and j.
Successive applications of eventual equality in the object colimit identify
all endpoints with the transitioned cospan objects. Eventual equality in the
arrow colimit makes the cone equation hold after a further transition.
The pullback is preserved by the composite transition from j, so its limiting
cone supplies a mediating arrow at this stage. Apply the cocone functor; its
transition equations and preservation of composition give both factorization
equations in V.pt. No uniqueness assertion is used here.

theorem filteredColimit_pullback_exists
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (j : J) {X Y Z : F.obj j} (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X) [HasPullback f g]
    (hpres : ∀ (k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (F.map a).toFunctor) :
    ∀ (W : V.pt) (a : W ⟶ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj Y)
      (b : W ⟶ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj Z),
      a ≫ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.map f = b ≫ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.map g →
      ∃ l : W ⟶ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj (pullback f g),
        l ≫ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.map (pullback.fst f g) = a ∧
        l ≫ (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.map (pullback.snd f g) = b
